title: 333-eDRAM - 3T Embedded DRAM Leveraging Monolithic 3D Integration of 3 Transistor Types: IGZO, Carbon Nanotube and Silicon FETs
problem: Embedded DRAM design faces fundamental trade-offs between high density, high retention time, high endurance, low access latency, low access energy, and low static leakage power. Traditional single-material DRAM cannot simultaneously optimize all of these dimensions.
motivation: The memory wall severely limits energy efficiency in computing systems; a new approach leveraging diverse material technologies can overcome the traditional trade-offs.
method: 333-eDRAM stacks three types of transistors in a single chip, each chosen for what it does best: IGZO transistors have nearly zero power drain when idle, so stored data lasts longer; Carbon Nanotube transistors push high current quickly, enabling fast data access; and Silicon transistors efficiently handle support circuits. The design jointly optimizes energy use, chip area, and access speed—metrics known together as EADP (energy-area-delay product)—at 7-nanometer scale. The researchers verified performance through cycle-accurate simulation and physics-based models calibrated to lab measurements.
key_novelty: Stacking three different transistor materials—IGZO, Carbon Nanotube, and Silicon—in a single 3D chip allows one memory design to achieve high density, long retention time, high endurance, fast speed, low power use, and minimal standby power drain all simultaneously, breaking the fundamental tradeoffs of traditional single-material DRAM.
contributions: 333-eDRAM architecture integrating three different FET types in monolithic 3D
1.96x better EDP than conventional silicon eDRAM
5.15x better EADP (energy-area-delay product) than conventional silicon eDRAM
Full physical layout designs demonstrating feasibility at 7nm technology node
primary_theme: Heterogeneous-material 3D integration for multi-objective eDRAM optimization
